factual_claims.claim: Static pruning methods are globally applied and irreversible, often leading to over-pruning, semantic loss, and an inability to adapt to new conversational contexts.
Bias in LLMs is a dynamic, accumulating phenomenon that propagates through priming, anaphora, and memory carry-over in multi-turn dialogues.

Dynamic Neuron Masking consistently reduces bias scores across multiple languages (Urdu, Punjabi, Pashto, Sindhi, Balochi) and task types compared to baseline models and other mitigation methods like pruning or steering vectors.
Dynamic neuron masking achieves a peak bias reduction of 0.439 at k=25 neurons, significantly outperforming random ablation strategies.
The LLM-as-a-Judge protocol shows strong agreement with human annotation, achieving a Spearman rank correlation of 0.74.

The proposed Dynamic Neuron Suppression framework introduces minimal latency, adding approximately 1.3ms per turn to the baseline forward pass, resulting in an end-to-end latency of roughly 28.5ms per turn.

Bias persists across diverse model architectures, including both open-source (Mistral, DeepSeek) and closed-source (GPT-4o, Claude) models, regardless of their specific training corpora or alignment strategies.
